answer: Each new key posts a walnut lock: a time-locked bond that unlocks only after it gathers eight chamber stamps along a protocol-chosen karst of randomized peer-routing hops, never self-selected. A public settlement atlas records every key's hop graph, stamp suppliers, and inter-stamp latency basin. If two keys share a hidden conduit — overlapping hop-subsets, reused stamp suppliers, or matched latency basins — the atlas flags the merge and slashes every walnut lock on that conduit in proportion to the cloned cluster, so mass-minted identities become a net loss.
